identity.title: Bedside walk / ambulatory desaturation and dyspnea reproduction test (hallway walk with pulse-ox, ability to complete)

technique.how: Record resting SpO2 and pulse, then walk the patient on a flat corridor at their own pace with continuous pulse oximetry and an escort for 2-6 minutes (or until symptoms). Record lowest SpO2, heart-rate rise, distance, whether the presenting symptom is reproduced, and whether the patient can complete the walk.
technique.prerequisites: Hemodynamically stable, ambulatory patient; reliable oximeter trace; staff escort and chair available.
technique.contraindications: Unstable angina or MI within days, resting SpO2 below target on maximal supplemental oxygen, uncontrolled arrhythmia, resting HR >120 or SBP >180/DBP >100 (ERS/ATS absolute/relative contraindications).

interpretation.positive_finding: Exertional desaturation (a fall in SpO2, commonly by >=4% or below 88-90%) or inability to complete the walk indicates a physiologic cause of dyspnea (parenchymal disease, PE, heart failure, anemia) and argues against isolated anxiety.
interpretation.negative_finding: A normal walk with stable SpO2 and no symptom reproduction lowers concern for significant gas-exchange impairment but does not exclude ACS, PE, or aortic stenosis.
interpretation.pitfalls: Motion artefact and poor perfusion produce false desaturation; the test is unstandardised at the bedside (pace, duration) and cut-offs are borrowed from chronic lung disease; results vary between repeat walks.
interpretation.changes_what: Desaturation or failure to complete: pursue objective testing (CT/echo/ABG) and reconsider discharge; normal walk: supports safe ambulation but does not replace diagnostic work-up.

sources.citation: Holland AE, Spruit MA, Troosters T, Puhan MA, Pepin V, Saey D, McCormack MC, Carlin BW, et al. An official European Respiratory Society/American Thoracic Society technical standard: field walking tests in chronic respiratory disease. Eur Respir J. 2014;44(6):1428-46.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not walk patients with suspected ACS, unstable arrhythmia, resting hypoxemia, or suspected severe aortic stenosis with exertional syncope.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Chest pain, presyncope, SpO2 <85%, or marked HR fall during the walk: stop immediately, seat the patient, apply oxygen, and reassess.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: The ERS/ATS standard notes results are sensitive to small methodological changes and recommends two tests for the 6MWT (Abstract); no bedside-walk reliability data found.

extraction_notes: No RCE, meta-analysis, or diagnostic-accuracy study of an informal inpatient/ED hallway walk was found; searches 'walk test emergency department dyspnea oxygen desaturation diagnostic accuracy' returned nothing and 'exertional desaturation[Title] emergency' returned only an ILD oxygen-response study (PMID 40395016, not a diagnostic-accuracy study). The ERS/ATS 2014 technical standard (confirmed PMID 25359355) is cited for procedure and contraindications only; specific SpO2 thresholds in the interpretation (>=4% fall, <88-90%) are conventional cut-offs (unverified recall) and not evidence of diagnostic accuracy. Record is not_quantified.
